title: Newly discovered "black hole star" could solve mystery of strange red dots spotted in the early universe
facts: Astronomers discovered a new class of astronomical object classified as a 'black hole star'.
The discovered black hole star produces 100 billion times more energy than any standard star.
The black hole star dates from approximately 660 million years after the Big Bang.
Astronomers observed the black hole star using the James Webb Space Telescope.
The study detailing the black hole star was published in the journal Nature on August 12, 2026.
Rohan Naidu of the University of Hawaii served as the lead author of the black hole star study.
Robert Simcoe from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology co-authored the research study.
Data analysis revealed that hydrogen gas makes the newly discovered object appear red.
Computer simulations determined the object is powered by a central black hole enclosed within a gas envelope.
Astronomers officially designated the discovered object as MoM-BH*-1.
MoM-BH*-1 produces light that completely outshines its host galaxy.
The James Webb Space Telescope detected oxygen-rich dust and water surrounding the evolved star IRS 3.
The star IRS 3 is located 0.55 light-years from the Milky Way's central supermassive black hole, Sagittarius A*.
Florian Peißker of the University of Cologne in Germany led the research team analyzing the star IRS 3.
Mid-infrared observations from the Webb telescope confirmed the presence of oxygen-rich silicate dust in IRS 3's envelope.
